Hong Kong Daqian International Enterprise Co., Ltd. v. Yu Qiumin and Haimen Daqian Thermal Power Co., Ltd. — dispute over a third-party revocation action

Ruling Summary

A third-party revocation action is an action brought against an effective judgment. On the one hand, it provides a remedy for a third party who, for some reason, was unable to participate in the proceedings and thus did not obtain procedural safeguards, yet may be bound by the effective judgment. On the other hand, it prevents the infringement of a third party's lawful rights and interests through a false lawsuit filed by others. In view of the res judicata effect and legal stability of an effective judgment, the issue of standing as a plaintiff in a third-party revocation action must strictly comply with the provisions of Article 56, Paragraph 3, of the Civil Procedure Law, i.e., the plaintiff initiating the revocation action must be a third party with an independent claim or a third party without an independent claim in the original case, and must also satisfy the other conditions set forth in that paragraph.

Supreme People's Court
Civil Ruling

(2016) Zui Gao Fa Min Shen No. 1045

Reapplying Applicant (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Hong Kong Daqian International Enterprise Co., Ltd. Domicile: Room C, 23rd Floor, Lucky Centre, 315-321 Lockhart Road, Wan Chai, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

Representative: Zhang Xianming, Director of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Shi Hongfei, Lawyer, Jiangsu Golden Great Wall Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Wang Rui, Lawyer, Jiangsu Golden Great Wall Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Yu Qiumin, female, Han Chinese, residing in Haimen City, Jiangsu Province.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Haimen Daqian Thermal Power Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 129 Dasheng Road, Sanchang Town, Haimen City, Jiangsu Province.

Representative: Liquidation Group of Haimen Daqian Thermal Power Co., Ltd., Administrator of the Company; Shi Bin, Head of the Administrator.

The reapplying applicant, Hong Kong Daqian International Enterprise Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hong Kong Daqian Company), dissatisfied with the civil ruling of the Jiangsu High People's Court (2015) Su Shang Che Zhong Zi No. 00010 in the dispute with respondents Yu Qiumin and Haimen Daqian Thermal Power Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Haimen Daqian Company) over a third-party revocation action, has filed an application for retrial with this Court. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law to review the matter, and the review has now been concluded.

Hong Kong Daqian Company applied for retrial with this Court, arguing: (1) The original ruling erred in finding that the result of the original case had no legal interest in the applicant and that the applicant was not a third party without an independent claim in the original case. The applicant is the wholly-owned shareholder of Haimen Daqian Company. The result of the original case caused Haimen Daqian Company to bear a huge debt without justification, which obviously damaged the interests of the shareholder, i.e., the applicant. (2) As the plaintiff in the original case, Yu Qiumin was also the adopted daughter of the actual controller of the defendant in the original case. To ensure the normal conduct of the trial and to avoid the appearance of a lawsuit by oneself against oneself, the People's Court should have notified the company's shareholders to participate in the proceedings as third parties. Moreover, the loans involved in the original case were all handled by Zhang Xianming, a director of the applicant. As an auxiliary third party to clarify the facts of the case, the applicant should also have participated in the proceedings of the original case. Due to the fault of Yu Qiumin, the People's Court did not notify the shareholders to participate in the proceedings in the original case, which infringed upon the lawful rights and interests of the applicant. Therefore, the applicant satisfies the subject-matter conditions for filing a third-party revocation action. (3) Even if the applicant does not meet the subject-matter conditions for a third-party revocation action, the parties in the original case acted in malicious collusion and illegally profited through false litigation, so the civil mediation document in the original case should also be revoked. The applicant requests a retrial of this case pursuant to Article 200, Item (6) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

Yu Qiumin submitted opinion: The applicant is a shareholder of Haimen Daqian Company, but Haimen Daqian Company is independent in legal personality. As to the company's property formed after the applicant's capital contribution, the company has independent rights of control and operation. For debts incurred in its actual business operations, the company should bear legal liability with its property. The applicant, as a shareholder, has no voting rights and cannot even interfere with the true expression of intent of Haimen Daqian Company regarding the repayment of debts. Therefore, the original ruling's finding that the applicant is not a third party without an independent claim is consistent with the principle of independent legal person property liability under the Company Law of the PRC. The applicant's application for retrial is requested to be dismissed.

Haimen Daqian Company submitted opinion: First, the subject matter of the private lending dispute filed by Yu Qiumin was Yu Qiumin's claim against Haimen Daqian Company. The applicant has no independent claim to this, so it is not a third party with an independent claim in the original case. Second, Haimen Daqian Company is an independent civil subject enjoying legal person property rights, and is capable of and should independently bear responsibility for its own actions. Hong Kong Daqian Company is a shareholder of Haimen Daqian Company, holding equity in the company, not property. The result of the original case has no legal interest relation with it, and it cannot participate in the original proceedings as a third party without an independent claim.

Opinion of the Court:

This case concerns a dispute over a third-party revocation action. A third-party revocation action is an action brought against an effective judgment. On the one hand, it provides a remedy for a third party who, for some reason, was unable to participate in the proceedings and thus did not obtain procedural safeguards, yet may be bound by the effective judgment. On the other hand, it prevents the infringement of a third party's lawful rights and interests through a false lawsuit filed by others. In view of the res judicata effect and legal stability of an effective judgment, the issue of standing as a plaintiff in a third-party revocation action must strictly comply with the provisions of Article 56, Paragraph 3, of the Civil Procedure Law, i.e., the plaintiff initiating the revocation action must be a third party with an independent claim or a third party without an independent claim in the original case, and must also satisfy the other conditions set forth in that paragraph. In this case, the subject matter of the original case was the private lending legal relationship between Yu Qiumin and Haimen Daqian Company. Although Hong Kong Daqian Company is the wholly-owned shareholder of Haimen Daqian Company, it has no independent claim to the subject matter of the original case, and the result of the original case would not cause it to bear any legal obligations or liabilities. Therefore, there is no legal interest between it and the result of the original case, and it is not a third party without an independent claim in the original case. Accordingly, Hong Kong Daqian Company has no right to file the third-party revocation action in this case. The original ruling dismissing its lawsuit was not improper. The grounds for Hong Kong Daqian Company's application for retrial are untenable. As to whether the directors or legal representative of Haimen Daqian Company acted ultra vires or engaged in related-party transactions harming the company's interests, the Company Law already provides remedies such as tort liability for directors and senior executives for the risks arising from the separation of company ownership and management. Hong Kong Daqian Company may seek relief accordingly.

In summary, the retrial application of Hong Kong Daqian Company does not meet the circumstances provided in Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. Pursuant to Article 204, Paragraph 1, of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 395, Paragraph 2, of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court hereby rules as follows:

The application for retrial by Hong Kong Daqian International Enterprise Co., Ltd. is dismissed.

Presiding Judge: Chen Jizhong

Judge: Shen Hongyu

Acting Judge: Ma Xiaoxu

August 26, 2016

Clerk: Zhang Bona
